text.p: Shareholders in Russia's third biggest oil producer Surgutneftegaz on Saturday approved a new company charter, dropping a five-percent limit to the number of foreign shareholders.
The new charter also bars shareholders from holding more than one percent of the votes.
"The maximum number of votes given to one company shareholder (together with affiliated representatives) cannot exceed one percent of the total number of voting shares", says the new charter.
The charter also says the restriction may be waived by the company's board of directors.
The company's shares in excess of one percent do not give their owners voting rights and do not qualify in the counting of the shareholders' general meeting quorum.
These restrictions also apply to the company's subsidiary, AO Surgutneftegaz, said the oil company's vice-president Natalia Olshanova.
She said more than five percent of AO Surgutneftegaz shares had been sold through American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) alone.
The clause giving the company a priority right to buy its shares has also been taken out of the charter, said Olshanskaya.
